newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pioneer seeks benchmark for domestic funds.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pioneer seeks benchmark for domestic funds.

text.p: The Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Company, owned by Boston-based Pioneer Group, seeks to create benchmarks to compare the performance of its mutal funds against those of the competition, the firm's head said.

"There's a necessity to define what the terminology (what each fund calls its products) means and such definitions are possible only when there's an indicator to which those funds can be compared," Alicja Malecka said. @
Malecka told a news conference on Monday that she hoped Pioneer and perhaps some of the other 13 fund companies in Poland would be able to work out benchmarks by the end of this year's first half.
She said Pioneer was currently preparing another fund which she would not comment on since it had not yet received Securities Commission (KPW) approval.

Malecka made the comments at a news conference devoted to Pioneer's lowering of the the maximum sales charge in its balanced and equity funds to 4.5 percent from 5.5 percent, with its bond fund highest sales charge slashed by half to two percent.
The new 4.5-percent and two-percent ceilings apply to investments of 5,000 zlotys and lower, compared to the previous 25,000 zlotys and lower. @

Investment Department head Jaroslaw Skorulski told the conference that there should still be stocks worth buying at mid-year despite the possible overall dampened demand caused by this year's busy primary market and parliamentary elections.
Pioneer also said it was adding an outlet in the cities of Katowice and Poznan, putting its number of own outlets to seven around the country. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
